comparisons.peer_topic: Future recognition of cash flow hedge net losses
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, the Firm expects approximately $(1.6) billion of after-tax net losses recorded in AOCI related to cash flow hedges to be recognized in income over the next 12 months, with terminated and open hedges having maximum recognition periods of approximately seven years tied to core lending and borrowing activities.
comparisons.comparison: BAC and JPM both report significant expected reclassifications of after-tax net *losses* from AOCI related to cash flow hedges within the next 12 months, which would negatively impact earnings. BAC expects $2.5 billion after-tax net losses to reclassify, while JPM expects approximately $1.6 billion after-tax net losses. BAC specifies that these losses are related to both open and closed hedges and primarily decrease net interest income. JPM provides further detail on the timing, noting that terminated hedges have a maximum recognition period of approximately seven years and that their longer-dated forecasted transactions relate to core lending and borrowing activities.
